title: Georgian Chronicles (Kartlis Tskhovreba: Targamos -> 8 Caucasian Sons -> Kings of Kartli -> Davidic Bagrationis), Al-Biruni (Parthians, Sasanians, 22 Afrighids, Himyarites) & Kebra Nagast Expansion

nodes.name: Targamos / Togarmah (Patriarch of All Caucasian Nations, Kartlis Tskhovreba)
nodes.era: Caucasian Table of Nations (Kartlis Tskhovreba pp. 13-18)
nodes.role: Patriarchal Origin of All Peoples of the Caucasus
nodes.notes: Targamos (Togarmah, lived 600 yrs between Mt. Ararat & Masis) divided the Caucasus among 8 sons (Haos, Kartlos, Bardos, Movak'an, Lek', Heros, K'avk'as, Egros) + Uobos.

nodes.name: Kartlos's Proto-Georgian Branch Anchor (Mtskhetos to Uplos)
nodes.role: Founders of Mtskheta, Kakheti, Gardabani, Uplistsikhe & Javakheti Anchor
nodes.notes: Bridge from Kartlos's sons Mtskhetos and Uplos down to King Parnavaz I of Kartli.

nodes.name: Kings of Iberia / Kartli Anchor (Pharnavazids, Nebrotids & Arshak'ids)
nodes.role: First Royal Dynasties of Georgia & Creator of Georgian Script Anchor
nodes.notes: Anchor linking Parnavaz I through Mirvan I (Nebrotid), Arshak' I, Parsman, and Aspagur to Abeshuru.

nodes.name: Chosroid (Mihranid-Sasanian) Dynasty Anchor (Mirian III to Vakht'ang Gorgasali)
nodes.role: Christianizers of Georgia & Founder of Tbilisi Anchor
nodes.notes: Mirian III (Mikhran, Sasanian prince + Abeshuru + St. Nino) -> Bakar -> Archil -> Vakht'ang I Gorgasali -> Dachi.

nodes.name: Bagrat'ioni Royal House Anchor (Sumbat Davitisdze Davidic Claim)
nodes.role: Longest-Reigning Christian Royal House (Davidic Claim Anchor)
nodes.notes: Unrolled person-by-person below from Bagrat' and Guaram I through Ashot' I, Bagrat' III, David IV, and Queen Tamar.

nodes.name: Parthian / Ashkanian Empire Anchor (Al-Biruni -> Kayanian Siyavush)
nodes.era: 247 BCE - 224 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 116-120; Betham Tab. CV)
nodes.role: 470-Year Iranian Superpower Bridged to Kayanian Siyavush
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 116) traces Ashk ben Ashkan (Arsaces I) directly back to Kayanian Prince Siyavush; unrolled individually in Wave 4.

nodes.name: Sasanian Empire Anchor (Al-Biruni Pedigree from Kay Bahman & Esfandiyar)
nodes.notes: Al-Biruni (p. 122) traces Ardashir I -> Babak -> Sasan -> Bahman -> Isfandiyar; unrolled person-by-person below.

nodes.name: Afrighid Shahs of Khwarazm Anchor (22 Generations in Al-Biruni)
nodes.role: Al-Biruni's Homeland Dynasty — 22 Unbroken Generations Anchor
nodes.notes: 22 unbroken father-to-son Khwarazmshahs from Afrigh (305 CE) to Abu 'Abdallah Muhammad (d. 995 CE), chained individually below.

nodes.name: Pre-Islamic Arab Kingdoms Anchor (Himyarite Tubbas, Lakhmids & Ghassanids)
nodes.era: c. 110 BCE - 636 CE (Al-Biruni pp. 40-50, 311, 384; Kebra Nagast Ch. 117)
nodes.role: Qahtanite / South Arabian & Syro-Mesopotamian Arab Monarchies Anchor
nodes.notes: Himyarite Tubbas, Lakhmid kings of Al-Hirah, and Christian Ghassanid kings of Syria.

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast Royal Court & Pre-Makeda Kings Anchor
nodes.era: c. 960 BCE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 22-48, Intro p. xxxv)
nodes.role: Bearers of the Ark of Zion from Jerusalem to Aksum Anchor
sources: Kebra Nagast (Budge 1922 Intro p. xxxv, Ch. 22-48, p. 62)
nodes.notes: 5 pre-Makeda kings, Merchant Tamrin, and High Priest 'Azaryas (son of Zadok) + 21 Israelite firstborn nobles.

nodes.name: Kebra Nagast World-Kingdoms Bridge ('Adrami, Fares & 'Akamhel)
nodes.role: Ethiopic Universal Bridge of Rome, Persia & Philistia to Israel
nodes.notes: Solomon's youngest son 'Adrami marries 'Adlonya to rule Rome; Perez (Fares) -> Persia; Samson + Delilah -> 'Akamhel.

nodes.name: Aksumite & Solomonic Restoration Anchor (King Kaleb -> Gabra Maskal -> Yekuno 'Amlak)
nodes.era: c. 520-1285 CE (Kebra Nagast Ch. 117 & Colophon, Budge pp. 225-229)
nodes.notes: King Kaleb defeated Himyarite Dhu-Nuwas in Yemen (525 CE); restored under Yekuno 'Amlak in 1270 CE.
